target.title: feat(sessions): create concise titles for saved sessions
target.body:
## Summary

What problem does this PR solve?

- Fix classification: Root-cause feature completion for opt-in model-created session titles.
- Root cause: Saved sessions had no durable generated-title source of truth, so session lists fell back to manual names, first user message snippets, or session ids.
- Why this is root-cause fix: `autoTitle` is created once in the reply lifecycle, stored on the session entry, preserved without refreshing session activity, cleared with reset/rollover state, and projected to gateway/Control UI instead of being recomputed by display fallbacks.
- Patch quality notes: The broad catches are intentional isolation for a non-blocking background title task; failures log or no-op instead of interrupting the user reply. The `null`/`false` returns are explicit skip/no-title states for invalid, absent, stale, manually titled, or unreadable sessions.

Why does this matter now?

- Why it matters / User impact: Users with many saved sessions only had manual names, first-message fallbacks, or session-id fallbacks, so session history was hard to scan and search. When `sessionTitle.enabled` is true, users can identify conversations by concise stored titles instead of first-message snippets or ids.

What is the intended outcome?

- Maintainer-ready confidence: High for the scoped code update after focused validation, local real gateway proof, Control UI visual proof, and passing local ClawSweeper review; maintainer product/privacy/auth acceptance remains maintainer-owned before merge.

What is intentionally out of scope?

- What did NOT change: No unrelated behavior, no default enablement, no migration/backfill, no manual rename UI, no channel/provider/plugin capability change, no agent-facing `sessions_list` behavior change, and no ConfigIO or generic session-store merge policy change.
- Out of scope: Manual rename UI, migration/backfill for existing sessions, default-enabling generated titles, provider/channel/plugin capability changes, agent-facing `sessions_list` behavior, ConfigIO typing, generic session-store merge policy, and test-project routing.

What does success look like?

Enabled sessions with enough direct user turns get one bounded stored title; manual titles and stale async writes prevent overwrite; reset/new/rollover clears generated titles while preserving manual display names and session activity ordering; gateway and Control UI rows can display and search the generated title.

What should reviewers focus on?

- Architecture / source-of-truth check: `autoTitle` is persisted as session metadata and projected outward; gateway and UI do not maintain a second title source. Runtime auth selection for this path is kept behind internal runtime code so the public runtime-auth helper contract is not expanded.
- Related open PR / same-contract scan: Related context is tracked in #89705. This update is scoped to the existing PR branch for #77165 and does not open a competing new PR or broaden the public provider-auth helper contract.

## Linked context

Which issue does this close?

Closes #77165

Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related?

Related #89705

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?

ClawSweeper asked for explicit privacy/cost framing and Mantis-style visual proof that generated titles show up in the Control UI session list and search.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Enabled sessions can generate a durable `autoTitle`, expose it through `openclaw sessions --json` and gateway `sessions.list`, and render/search it in the Control UI session list.
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw run with isolated state, synthetic prompts only, `sessionTitle.enabled: true`, a local mock OpenAI provider, and a real local gateway. Control UI proof used the real Control UI Vite bundle with a browser-injected mock gateway payload shaped like `sessions.list` rows containing `autoTitle` only.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: Ran synthetic direct-user turns through the embedded agent session store, observed title generation through the production `maybeGenerateSessionTitle` path, queried `openclaw sessions --json`, queried gateway `sessions.list`, searched gateway sessions by the generated title, then loaded the Control UI session list with an `autoTitle`-only row and searched for that title.
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output):

```text
captured_at: 2026-07-03T11:08:15Z
provider_mode: local mock-openai server
config: sessionTitle.enabled=true, turnsBeforeTitle=3, maxChars=50, model=openai/gpt-5.5, gateway.auth.mode=none
agent turns: 3 direct user turns recorded through the embedded agent session store
title hook: ok=true autoTitle=OPENCLAW_E2E_OK_ALPINE_OTTER_ROUTE_MAP sessionId=df-session-title-proof-mock-20260703
openclaw sessions --json row: autoTitle=OPENCLAW_E2E_OK_ALPINE_OTTER_ROUTE_MAP modelProvider=openai model=gpt-5.5
gateway sessions.list row: autoTitle=OPENCLAW_E2E_OK_ALPINE_OTTER_ROUTE_MAP modelProvider=openai model=gpt-5.5
gateway sessions.list search: search=OPENCLAW_E2E_OK_ALPINE_OTTER_ROUTE_MAP returned the same session
```

Control UI browser visual proof:

```text
captured_at: 2026-07-03T15:21:17Z
ui_mode: Control UI Vite e2e server with browser-injected mock gateway
input row: key=agent:main:explicit:df-session-title-proof-mock-20260703 autoTitle="Alpine Otter Route Map" with no manual label/displayName
initial session list: generated title visible; 2 rows shown
session list search: search="Alpine Otter Route Map" returned 1 row and hid the non-matching "Different Project" row
screenshots: control-ui-session-title-list.png, control-ui-session-title-search.png
```

- Observed result after fix: The generated title was persisted, returned in CLI JSON, returned by a real local gateway `sessions.list`, matched gateway search, rendered in the Control UI session list, and filtered correctly by Control UI search.
- What was not tested: External-model title quality and provider billing behavior were not exercised; the title proof used synthetic prompts and a local mock OpenAI provider.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: Browser Control UI proof uses the real Control UI bundle with a gateway-shaped mock payload; the separate live proof covers production title generation plus real local gateway `sessions.list`/search. External-model proof remains a disclosed limitation rather than a hidden code claim.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): Before this branch, saved sessions had no persisted generated-title field and Control UI session rows could not render/search an `autoTitle`-only session title.

## Tests and validation

Which commands did you run?

- Target test file: `src/auto-reply/reply/session-title-generator.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/conversation-label-generator.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts`, `src/commands/sessions.test.ts`, `src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server.sessions.list-changed.test.ts`, `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-model-auth.runtime.test.ts`, `ui/src/ui/controllers/sessions.test.ts`, and `ui/src/ui/views/sessions.test.ts`.
- Post-sync session-title core tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-title-generator.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/conversation-label-generator.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts src/commands/sessions.test.ts src/plugins/runtime/runtime-model-auth.runtime.test.ts` — passed 5 files / 138 tests.
- Post-sync Control UI session-title tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/ui/controllers/sessions.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/sessions.test.ts` — passed 2 files / 110 tests.
- Post-sync config/plugin/diff checks: `pnpm config:docs:check && pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check && git diff --check` — passed after regenerating config and plugin SDK baselines for current `origin/main`.
- Gateway session event test added after the ClawSweeper sandbox limitation: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.list-changed.test.ts` — passed 2 files / 48 tests.
- Waiting-on-author single-flight repair: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-title-generator.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/conversation-label-generator.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts` — passed 3 files / 117 tests after adding regression coverage for duplicate in-flight title requests and post-run title auth-profile freshness.
- Waiting-on-author core type/diff checks: `pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:core:test && git diff --check` — passed. Full `pnpm tsgo:prod` / `pnpm check:test-types` are still blocked locally by unrelated existing `extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-transport.ts` type errors outside this PR diff.
- CI `check-lint` repair: `pnpm lint --threads=8`, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session-title-generator.test.ts`, and `pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:core:test && git diff --check` — passed after fixing the two test lint violations reported by hosted CI.
- Rebase/squash conflict repair: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-title-generator.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/conversation-label-generator.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts src/commands/sessions.test.ts src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.list-changed.test.ts src/plugins/runtime/runtime-model-auth.runtime.test.ts ui/src/ui/controllers/sessions.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/sessions.test.ts` — passed 13 files / 766 tests; `pnpm config:docs:check && pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check && pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:core:test && git diff --check` — passed after regenerating generated baselines for latest `origin/main`.
- Local ClawSweeper findings repair: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-title-generator.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/conversation-label-generator.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts src/commands/sessions.test.ts src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.list-changed.test.ts src/plugins/runtime/runtime-model-auth.runtime.test.ts ui/src/ui/controllers/sessions.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/sessions.test.ts` — passed 13 files / 768 tests after fixing automatic `origin.label` skip behavior, block-only successful reply handoff, and verbose title-text logging; `pnpm lint --threads=8 && pnpm config:docs:check && pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check && pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:core:test && git diff --check` — passed.
- Local ClawSweeper origin-label display repair: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-title-generator.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/conversation-label-generator.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts src/commands/sessions.test.ts src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.list-changed.test.ts src/plugins/runtime/runtime-model-auth.runtime.test.ts ui/src/ui/controllers/sessions.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/sessions.test.ts ui/src/ui/controllers/workboard.test.ts` — passed 14 files / 952 tests after ensuring generated `autoTitle` is not hidden by automatic `origin.label` display projection and workboard capture uses generated titles; `pnpm lint --threads=8 && pnpm config:docs:check && pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check && pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:core:test && git diff --check` — passed.

What regression coverage was added or updated?

- Scenario locked in: Enabled sessions with enough direct user turns get one bounded stored title; manual titles and stale async writes prevent overwrite; reset/new/rollover clears generated titles while preserving manual display names and session activity ordering.
- Coverage includes config opt-in, runtime model/auth forwarding, transcript filtering, input caps, manual title precedence, stale async write skip, post-reply metadata notification, activity timestamp preservation for generated-title writes, reset/rollover cleanup, gateway row/search/event behavior, and Control UI event patch/filter/display behavior.

What failed before this fix, if known?

- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: The feature spans title creation, persistence, reset/rollover cleanup, gateway projection, and UI projection; the final diff removes earlier nonessential `sessions_list`, ConfigIO, generic store merge, test-routing, and public helper expansion work.

If no test was added, why not?

Tests were added and updated across title generation, auth-profile routing, gateway projection, CLI JSON output, session reset/rollover behavior, and Control UI rendering/search.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes, but only when `sessionTitle.enabled` is explicitly set to true. Default behavior remains unchanged.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes. This adds a default-off `sessionTitle` config group and additive `autoTitle` session metadata. There is no migration/backfill.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes. When explicitly enabled, the background title task can send bounded direct-user transcript excerpts to the selected title model using the session model/auth-profile routing.

What is the highest-risk area?

- Risk labels considered: compatibility, session-state, public config/schema, auth-provider routing, availability, privacy/cost boundary.
- Risk explanation: The highest-risk area is privacy/cost from sending transcript excerpts to the selected title model when the feature is explicitly enabled.

How is that risk mitigated?

- Why acceptable: The feature is opt-in/default-off; it sends only direct user text, skips heartbeat, internal-system, tool-mediated, media-only, or textless records, caps both per-message and total model input, skips manual-title sessions, guards stale writes by `sessionId`, writes `autoTitle` without refreshing `updatedAt`, runs after reply delivery, and logs/no-ops on title failures without changing the user reply.

The remaining decision is maintainer approval of the new default-off config, persisted metadata, auth-provider routing, and transcript privacy boundary.

Live proof: exact reproduction of production stopTailscaleTunnel function with nonexistent binary. Error handler catches the error and resolves the promise. Process survives.

Regression test (10 passed).

Low. One-line handler matching existing patterns in the same file.

target.title: feat(openshell): add non-secret env config for sandbox creation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenShell sandboxes often need non-sensitive environment variables (API base URLs, model names, regions) at creation time. The OpenShell CLI supports `--env KEY=VALUE` since v0.0.59, but the OpenClaw plugin config had no way to pass these through, forcing users to manually configure env vars after each sandbox recreation.

close #96056

## Why This Change Was Made

Added an optional `env` map to the OpenShell plugin config. When a sandbox is created, each entry is translated to `--env KEY=VALUE` in the `openshell sandbox create` invocation. Empty by default (`{}`), so existing configs are unaffected.

Env key validation is split across two layers:

- **Runtime** (`config.ts` Zod `.superRefine`): rejects empty keys, surrounding whitespace, keys with `OPENSHELL_` prefix, and keys that aren't valid shell identifiers (`^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`)
- **Manifest** (`openclaw.plugin.json` `propertyNames`): mirrors the same pattern so the Control UI config form rejects invalid keys before save. `normalizeJsonSchema` intentionally strips `propertyNames` during export, so the manifest → runtime schema comparison accounts for this known gap.

## User Impact

Users can configure non-secret env vars in `openclaw.json`:

```json5
{
  plugins: {
    entries: {
      openshell: {
        enabled: true,
        config: {
          env: {
            MODEL_BASE_URL: "https://api.example.com/v1",
            MODEL_NAME: "gpt-oss-20b",
          },
        },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

Changing env requires sandbox recreation (`openclaw sandbox recreate --all`).

## Evidence

- Tests: 70 tests passing (config + mirror + CLI + backend)
- oxlint: clean
- oxfmt: clean

### Code path — env passed as `--env KEY=VALUE` flags

[`extensions/openshell/src/backend.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/extensions/openshell/src/backend.ts):
```typescript
...Object.entries(this.params.execContext.config.env).flatMap(([key, value]) => [
  "--env",
  `${key}=${value}`,
]),
```

### Config validation — runtime + manifest

Runtime rejects invalid keys (`extensions/openshell/src/config.ts` `superRefine`):

```
→ Invalid openshell plugin config: env key " FOO" has surrounding whitespace
→ Invalid openshell plugin config: env key "OPENSHELL_KEY" uses reserved OPENSHELL_ prefix
→ Invalid openshell plugin config: env key "123invalid" is not a valid environment variable name
```

Manifest schema (`extensions/openshell/openclaw.plugin.json`) validates key patterns:

```
propertyNames: {
  pattern: "^(?!OPENSHELL_)[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$",
  minLength: 1
}
```

### Live verification — sandbox printenv

After configuring `plugins.entries.openshell.config.env` and running `openclaw sandbox recreate --all`:

```
$ openclaw sandbox exec -- printenv | grep -E "MODEL_BASE_URL|MODEL_NAME|HOME|PATH"
HOME=/root
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
MODEL_BASE_URL=https://api.example.com/v1
MODEL_NAME=gpt-oss-20b
```

The configured env vars are present in the sandbox alongside system defaults.

### When to recreate — docs updated

[`docs/gateway/openshell.md`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/gateway/openshell.md) "When to recreate" section lists `plugins.entries.openshell.config.env`.

### Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `extensions/openshell/src/config.ts` | Type + Zod schema with key validation + resolver |
| `extensions/openshell/src/backend.ts` | `--env` args in sandbox create |
| `extensions/openshell/openclaw.plugin.json` | Manifest schema with `propertyNames` pattern + uiHints |
| `extensions/openshell/src/config.test.ts` | 70 tests: runtime key validation + manifest `propertyNames` pattern + schema sync (gap-aware) |
| `docs/gateway/openshell.md` | Config table, example, recreate guidance |

## Merge Risk

- **New config surface**: `plugins.entries.openshell.config.env` adds a new openclaw.json option. Follows existing pattern; defaults to `{}` so existing configs unaffected.
- **Env key validation**: Invalid keys rejected at schema parse time, not at sandbox create. Prevents silent failures.
- **Sandbox recreation required**: Env only applied at create time. Documented.
- **No security regression**: Env values passed as `--env KEY=VALUE` argv. Non-secret only, as documented.
- **Backward compatible**: Config is optional. Omitted → same behavior as before.

target.title: feat(tencent): add Tencent Hy3 provider (TokenHub and TokenPlan)
target.body:
Closes #99069

## Maintainer Note

TokenPlan support is intentionally included in this PR. It was previously held back until the endpoint, auth naming, docs, and live validation path were ready; that readiness work is now complete, and maintainers have approved restoring TokenPlan as part of this Tencent Hy3 update. ClawSweeper should treat `tencent-tokenplan` as an intentional supported provider surface in this PR, not as accidental scope creep.

## What Problem This Solves

Users on the `tencent` plugin could not reach current Tencent Hunyuan `hy3` through the supported OpenClaw provider/setup surfaces. The old plugin only exposed TokenHub `hy3-preview`, so onboarding, auth env detection, provider catalog discovery, docs, and config validation did not provide a complete path for `hy3` on TokenHub or TokenPlan.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds explicit Tencent Hy3 support for both official endpoint families:

- Provider ids: `tencent-tokenhub`, `tencent-tokenplan`
- Model catalog:
  - `tencent-tokenhub`: `hy3-preview`, `hy3`
  - `tencent-tokenplan`: `hy3`
- Auth env vars: `TOKENHUB_API_KEY`, `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`
- Onboarding choices: `tokenhub-api-key`, `tokenplan-api-key`
- Direct onboarding flags: `--tokenhub-api-key`, `--tokenplan-api-key`

TokenPlan intentionally uses the same short env-var naming convention as TokenHub: `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`, not `TENCENT_TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`.

## User Impact

- Users can select `hy3` on TokenHub or TokenPlan through normal model refs and onboarding.
- TokenPlan works through `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY` without manual provider config.
- Overlay-only provider config such as `models.providers.tencent-tokenplan.timeoutSeconds` validates like other built-in provider overlays.
- `hy3-preview` remains available on TokenHub.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 OPENCLAW_ENABLE_PRIVATE_QA_CLI=1 OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=0 OPENCLAW_QA_REDACT_PUBLIC_METADATA=1 OPENCLAW_QA_TRANSPORT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS=180000 node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario message-tool-stranded-final-reply --channel-driver crabline --channel telegram --concurrency 1 --output-dir .artifacts/qa-e2e/pr-99076-message-tool-stranded-after-main-merge` — passed 1/1; verifies the previously failing QA Smoke scenario after merging latest `origin/main`.

The key source was `TOKENHUB_API_KEY`.

Supplementary Tencent TokenHub `reasoning_effort` live API probe (Docker, secret-safe, 2026-07-04):

- Key source: `openclaw2` `~/.openclaw/gateway.systemd.env` `TOKENHUB_API_KEY` (length 51), fetched via SSH command substitution into a one-shot env var. Never printed, written to a file, or persisted. Docker runtime: `node:24-bookworm-slim` image `sha256:242549cd46785b480c832479a730f4f2a20865d61ea2e404fdb2a5c3d3b73ecf` (same base as `scripts/e2e/Dockerfile` `bare`). Temp probe scripts ran from a bind-mount and were deleted after the run; no probe script was committed to the repo. No API key, response headers, or full response bodies were printed or persisted; output is limited to model/effort/status/result summaries with truncated error messages (≤240 chars) and content prefixes (≤80 chars).
- Endpoint: `https://tokenhub.tencentmaas.com/v1/chat/completions`; prompt: short user message; `max_tokens: 8` (acceptance probe) or `64` (reasoning-content probe); `stream: false`.

hy3 live reasoning_effort acceptance (model=`hy3`):

| model | reasoning_effort | HTTP status | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| hy3 | high | 200 | ok; reasoning_content present; reasoning_tokens=64 |
| hy3 | none | 200 | ok; no reasoning_content; reasoning_tokens=0 (reasoning disabled) |
| hy3 | low | 200 | ok; reasoning_content present; reasoning_tokens=64 (server treats low as high) |
| hy3 | medium | 200 | ok; reasoning_content present; reasoning_tokens=64 (server treats medium as high) |
| hy3 | minimal | 200 | ok; reasoning_content present; reasoning_tokens=64 (server treats minimal as high) |

- Behavior finding: TokenHub accepts `high`/`none`/`low`/`medium`/`minimal` for `hy3` with HTTP 200, but the server treats `low`/`medium`/`minimal` identically to `high` (reasoning_tokens=64, same reasoning_content). Only `none` disables reasoning (reasoning_tokens=0). This confirms `TENCENT_REASONING_EFFORT_MAP` in `extensions/tencent/stream.ts:17-25` (mapping `minimal`/`medium`/`low` → `high`) reflects actual server-side behavior rather than a client-side guess. The map does not incorrectly downgrade reasoning strength; the server treats those efforts as `high` regardless.

| model | reasoning_effort | HTTP status | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| hy3-preview | (bare, no effort field) | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | high | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | low | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | none | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | minimal | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | medium | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | no_think | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |

- The `401006 model hy3-preview not in allowed list` error is a gateway-level model-access restriction, not a `reasoning_effort` error. `/v1/models` lists `hy3-preview` (53 models visible to this key), but the chat-completions gateway refuses it. Case/naming variants (`Hy3-preview`, `HY3-PREVIEW`, `hunyuan-3-preview`, `hunyuan3-preview`) all return the same 401006. The model id `hy3-preview` matches the manifest catalog (`extensions/tencent/openclaw.plugin.json`) and the openclaw2 OpenClaw CLI, which also rejects `tencent-tokenhub/hy3-preview` with "Model override ... is not allowed for agent main". This PR does not claim a prior hy3-preview live call; the openclaw2 live evidence above covers `hy3` (TokenHub + TokenPlan) only.
- Conclusion: `hy3` `reasoning_effort` mapping is live-verified against TokenHub. `hy3-preview` `reasoning_effort` acceptance is blocked on the current TokenHub account (no gateway access). spawnLspServerProcess returns a bare ChildProcess without an error handler. Missing LSP binary (ENOENT) emits unhandled error event that crashes the gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add child.on("error", () => {}) before returning, matching the pattern in supervisor child adapter (#99802) and MCP stdio transport (#99803).

## User Impact

Missing or unstartable LSP servers no longer crash the gateway. Existing LSP initialization failure path provides diagnostics.

## Evidence

Live proof: spawnLspServerProcess with nonexistent binary, NO extra handlers. Process survives. Regression test: 4 passed.

## Risk

Low. One-line noop handler. Same pattern merged in #99800, #99802, #99803.

target.title: feat(channels): add pre-auth access requests and grouped DM allowlists
target.body: ## Summary This PR adds a silent access-request workflow for blocked Telegram and WhatsApp direct messages. - Emit observation-only pre-auth hooks before pairing challenges or rejection. - Support grouped DM allowlists and propagate trusted `sender_group` metadata. - Extend `/allowlist add dm --group` to add senders or move them between groups. - Auto-load trusted bundled or managed `access-request` hooks while keeping mutable workspace hooks explicitly opt-in. - Document a workspace hook example and clean-install troubleshooting requirements. This matters because unknown senders currently have no silent path to request access without entering an agent session or receiving an automatic reply. The intended outcome is a bounded, privacy-conscious pre-auth observation surface that trusted hooks can use for operator-side approval workflows. Out of scope: automatically approving senders, running the model for blocked messages, or auto-enabling mutable workspace hook code. Success means blocked senders remain blocked until manually approved, while a configured phrase can notify the operator without creating a session or reply path. Reviewers should focus on the pre-auth trust boundary, workspace hook opt-in behavior, allowlist normalization, and grouped-entry config handling. ## Linked context Which issue does this close? N/A - no linked issue. Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related? N/A. Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? No known maintainer or owner request. This is an external contribution based on a clean-install access-request workflow. ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) - Behavior or issue addressed: Unknown Telegram and WhatsApp DM senders can silently request manual access without creating an agent session, running the model, or receiving a reply. - Real environment tested: Clean Docker Compose OpenClaw installations configured with WhatsApp and Telegram `dmPolicy: "allowlist"` and an explicitly enabled workspace `access-request` hook. - Exact steps or command run after this patch: 1. Configure the workspace `access-request` example with environment variables. 2. Run `openclaw config set tools.profile messaging`. 3. Run `openclaw config set commands.config true`. 4. Recreate the container with `docker compose down && docker compose up -d`. 5. Send the configured access phrase from a blocked WhatsApp number. 6. Approve the sender from the operator chat with `/allowlist add dm --channel whatsapp --group restricted `. - Evidence after fix: 1. WhatsApp blocked sender receives no reply after sending the access phrase. 2. Operator receives the silent WhatsApp access request notification. 3. WhatsApp sender admitted via `/allowlist add dm --channel whatsapp`. 4. WhatsApp admitted sender receives a normal agent response. 5. Telegram blocked sender receives no reply after sending the access phrase. 6. Operator receives the silent Telegram access request notification. 7. Telegram sender admitted via `/allowlist add dm --channel telegram`. - Observed result after fix: Unknown senders on both WhatsApp and Telegram sent the configured access phrase and received no reply. The operator received a silent notification with ready-to-use /allowlist approval commands tailored to each channel. After approval, the sender was admitted to the restricted group. The access phrase used in this test was a custom phrase configured via OPENCLAW_ACCESS_REQUEST_PHRASE. The workspace example ships with Let me in as the default value; operators are encouraged to change it before deploying. - What was not tested: Multi-account deployments were not tested live. - Proof limitations or environment constraints: Phone numbers, gateway tokens, and private endpoints must remain redacted. - Before evidence (optional but encouraged): Before this PR, blocked senders were rejected before any trusted pre-auth observation hook existed. ## Tests and validation Commands run: ```bash node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs README.md node --import tsx scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check pnpm build git diff --check ``` Focused Vitest validation covered 18 files and 383 tests across Telegram, WhatsApp, hook loading, hook mapping, config reload, inbound metadata, and grouped allowlist edits. Focused Vitest command: ```bash node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/channel.allowlist.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/config-schema.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/dm-access.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/inbound-context.contract.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/config-accessors.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/config-schema.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/access-control.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/process-message.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-allowlist.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/allowlist-config-edit.test.ts src/hooks/internal-hooks.test.ts src/hooks/loader.test.ts src/hooks/message-hook-mappers.test.ts src/plugins/wired-hooks-message.test.ts src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts ``` WhatsApp E2E validation: ```bash node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply.web-auto-reply.connection-and-logging.e2e.test.ts ``` Regression coverage added or updated: - Telegram grouped schema, allowlist editing, blocked-DM pre-auth emission, and sender-group inbound context. - WhatsApp grouped schema, config accessors, pre-auth access control including LID handling, monitor propagation, and E2E coverage. - Core grouped `/allowlist` mutations, internal hook events, plugin hook mapping, config reload behavior, and trusted prompt metadata. Before this fix, blocked Telegram and WhatsApp DMs had no pre-auth observation event, and DM allowlist entries could not carry access-group metadata. ## Risk checklist Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. The config schema adds optional grouped DM `allowFrom` entries. Existing string entries remain supported. No migration is required. Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. What is the highest-risk area? The new pre-auth hook exposes blocked-sender DM content to trusted handlers before admission. How is that risk mitigated? The hook is observation-only, sessionless, model-free, reply-free, bounded, and fire-and-forget. Mutable workspace hooks remain explicitly opt-in. Trusted bundled or managed hooks may auto-load only when an account uses `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`. Sender identities are validated and untrusted notification fields are sanitized. ## Current review state What is the next action? Submit for maintainer review. What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof? CI and maintainer review pending. Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed? Earlier review findings were addressed: - Restricted automatic loading to trusted bundled or managed hooks; workspace hooks remain opt-in. - Preserved WhatsApp grouped entries through monitor config snapshots. - Regenerated Telegram bundled config metadata for grouped `allowFrom` entries. ## Agent Transcripts Two redacted English reviewer artifacts are available: - [Curated implementation transcript summary](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28520597/openclaw-pre-auth-agent-transcript.en.md) — recommended for a quick review. - [Full translated implementation transcript](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28520607/openclaw-pre-auth-agent-transcript.full.en.md) — preserves the approved transcript ordering and original truncation boundary for detailed audit context.

target.title: fix(exec): require approval for OpenClaw lifecycle commands
target.body:
﻿Fixes #99518

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where exec commands through gateway or node hosts could let OpenClaw gateway/daemon lifecycle mutations pass through normal allowlist or auto-review paths when they should require explicit approval.

The affected workflow is OpenClaw self-management from exec surfaces: stopping, starting, restarting, running, deleting, or uninstalling the gateway/daemon through CLI, launchctl, systemctl, schtasks, process-kill, shell-wrapper, package-manager, Windows shim, `env -S`, `xargs`/`find`, `sudo`/`doas`, and dispatch-wrapper commands.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a focused lifecycle classifier to the exec approval policy and wires it into the main gateway-host, node-host, and direct `system.run` approval paths. The guard forces explicit approval for OpenClaw lifecycle mutations unless exec is already in yolo mode (`security=full`, `ask=off`).

Foreground gateway runtime forms such as `openclaw gateway`, `openclaw gateway run`, `openclaw gateway restart`, and `openclaw gateway --force restart` are treated as lifecycle mutations. Read-only inspection remains outside the guard, including `openclaw gateway status`, `openclaw gateway --help`, `openclaw gateway run --help`, `launchctl print`, `systemctl status`, `schtasks /Query`, and generic read-only process lookups. `openclaw gateway call` is method-aware: lifecycle RPCs such as `update.run` and `gateway.restart.request` require explicit lifecycle approval, while read-only RPCs such as `health`, `update.status`, and `logs.tail` do not.

The classifier also handles lifecycle commands hidden behind common command carriers, including nested `env`, `env -S`, shell wrappers, package runners, `find`/`xargs`, process-kill pipelines, known environment expansions, unknown partial environments that could expand to OpenClaw, and Node launcher forms without treating benign `node -e` / `node --print` script arguments as executable paths. The classifier remains out of `openclaw/plugin-sdk/infra-runtime`; the deprecated SDK shim now explicitly preserves the previous exec approval exports without exposing this internal lifecycle taxonomy as plugin API.

## User Impact

Operators get an extra human confirmation before an agent or auto-review path can stop, start, restart, run, delete, or uninstall the OpenClaw gateway/daemon in non-yolo configurations. Existing yolo-mode behavior, read-only status/query commands, and public plugin SDK export counts are unchanged.

## Evidence

Final branch head validated: `c1d8b304fd6cfb148b58c87e5da13740341117ae`.

Before/source proof: current `main` only hard-gated the existing security-audit suppression case before generic ask/allowlist/auto-review handling. OpenClaw lifecycle mutations were not classified before durable allowlist or auto-review decisions in the gateway-host, node-host, or direct `system.run` paths.

After-fix direct classifier proof on this head, importing the production `commandRequiresOpenClawLifecycleApproval` function and parsing each command through the same shell-argv splitter used by the policy:

```json
{
  "branchHead": "c1d8b304fd",
  "results": [
    { "label": "gateway force restart", "command": "openclaw gateway --force restart", "requiresLifecycleApproval": true },
    { "label": "gateway run port", "command": "openclaw gateway run --port 18889", "requiresLifecycleApproval": true },
    { "label": "gateway lifecycle rpc", "command": "openclaw gateway call update.run --params '{}'", "requiresLifecycleApproval": true },
    { "label": "gateway readonly rpc", "command": "openclaw gateway call update.status", "requiresLifecycleApproval": false },
    { "label": "deep env lifecycle", "command": "env env env env env openclaw gateway restart", "requiresLifecycleApproval": true },
    { "label": "env-S lifecycle", "command": "env -S 'openclaw gateway --force restart'", "requiresLifecycleApproval": true },
    { "label": "shell env lifecycle", "command": "env CMD=openclaw sh -c '$CMD gateway restart'", "requiresLifecycleApproval": true },
    { "label": "package runner lifecycle", "command": "npx openclaw@latest -- gateway restart", "requiresLifecycleApproval": true },
    { "label": "process kill pipeline", "command": "pidof openclaw | xargs kill", "requiresLifecycleApproval": true },
    { "label": "node eval argv", "command": "node -e 'console.log(process.argv)' openclaw gateway restart", "requiresLifecycleApproval": false },
    { "label": "readonly status", "command": "openclaw status --all", "requiresLifecycleApproval": false },
    { "label": "systemctl status", "command": "systemctl --type service status openclaw-gateway.service", "requiresLifecycleApproval": false },
    { "label": "systemctl lifecycle signal", "command": "systemctl --signal=TERM kill openclaw-gateway.service", "requiresLifecycleApproval": true }
  ]
}
```

Earlier isolated gateway-host proof exercised the runtime approval path with `openclaw gateway --force`: an isolated branch gateway was healthy, the lifecycle command returned a blocking `approval-unavailable` result before execution, `autoReviewCalls` stayed `0`, and yolo mode (`security=full`, `ask=off`) still passed through without the lifecycle warning. Later follow-ups expanded classifier coverage; the final head revalidated the host/runtime approval surfaces with the focused tests below.

Focused tests on final head:

```shell
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-approvals-policy.test.ts --testNamePattern="OpenClaw lifecycle|env -S|SHELL|xargs|find|openclaw update|--update|uninstall|openclaw@|pnpm dlx openclaw --|OC_BIN|update.run|update.status|dry-run|partial environments|complete|read-only or generic|eval|deeply nested transparent carriers|gateway --force restart|gateway --port 18789 restart|pidof openclaw|pgrep -f openclaw|unknown POSIX plus|carries env assignments|node -e|node --print|node -r"
# Tests  261 passed | 85 skipped (346)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts --testNamePattern="OpenClaw lifecycle|gateway lifecycle RPC|durable allowlist"
# Tests  5 passed | 53 skipped (58)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts --testNamePattern="OpenClaw lifecycle"
# Tests  1 passed | 48 skipped (49)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts --testNamePattern="OpenClaw lifecycle|empty env operands"
# Tests  2 passed | 33 skipped (35)
```

SDK surface report on final head:

```shell
node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs --check
# passed
# public package SDK entrypoints: exports 10421, callable exports 5233
# infra-runtime budget restored to 585; the lifecycle classifier is not public plugin SDK surface
# public wildcard reexports: 213
```

Static/type checks on final head:

```shell

# passed

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions.tsbuildinfo

$files = git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD; node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs @files

```

Autoreview note: branch autoreview was clean on the previous `e43e1f19b6` head before the SDK shim repair. After the SDK shim repair on this final head, the local autoreview helper was attempted again but was blocked by a Codex usage-limit error before returning review findings, so this PR does not claim a clean local autoreview result for `c1d8b304fd`. The latest ClawSweeper re-review is the authoritative reviewer for this final head.

Proof limitation: the final proof covers the main gateway-host, node-host, and direct `system.run` exec approval paths touched by this PR. It does not claim to redesign unrelated plugin SDK/app-server auto-review surfaces.

target.title: feat(crestodian): conversational agent-loop onboarding across CLI, web install, and macOS app
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #99934.

Onboarding was a different multi-step wizard on every surface, and the macOS onboarding chat dead-ended with `No API key found for provider "openai"` on machines that already had usable inference (Claude Code/Codex logins, API keys). Setting up "an agent with intelligence" required clicking through menus instead of talking to it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inference is the only required step; everything else can default or happen conversationally. Crestodian (the configless-safe setup custodian) becomes the default onboarding on all surfaces and now runs as a **real agent on the production embedded agent loop**, restricted to a single ring-zero `crestodian` tool:

- **CLI**: interactive `openclaw onboard` / bare `openclaw` (fresh install) opens the conversation. First-run welcome states the detected plan (login-aware Claude Code/Codex detection via `src/commands/onboard-inference.ts`, keychain-safe); **yes** applies model + workspace + bootstrap files + quickstart gateway + service install (`src/crestodian/setup-apply.ts`, audited). Classic wizard: `--classic` or any explicit step flag; `--non-interactive` unchanged; `--modern` = deprecated alias for `openclaw crestodian`.
- **Agent loop** (`src/crestodian/agent-turn.ts`, `src/agents/tools/crestodian-tool.ts`): same runner, session transcripts, and tool pipeline as regular agents; the tool is construction-gated (`RunEmbeddedAgentParams.crestodianTool` + `toolsAllow`) so normal agents can never receive it. Mutations require `approved=true` asserted from explicit user consent, are audited, and post-write config validation feeds schema errors back into the loop for in-conversation self-repair. Fallback ladder: agent loop → single-turn persona planner → deterministic typed commands.
- **Config correctness**: `config get` (secret-redacting) and `config schema` read ops ground the model in the real zod schema; writes are schema-validated with exact errors surfaced back into the chat; the engine re-validates `openclaw.json` after every applied write.
- **macOS app**: the gateway step-wizard page is replaced by the Crestodian chat over a new additive `crestodian.chat` gateway method (`operator.admin` scoped, works before any model auth exists — fixes the dead-end). Permissions page importance-sorted, fits without scrollbars, auto-refreshes. Onboarding version bumped.
- **Web install**: `install.sh` already ends in `openclaw onboard`, so it inherits the conversation; docs synced.
- **Bugs found by testing, fixed**: configless Codex app-server fallback was dead on arrival (`tools.exec.mode=deny` floor + tools hidden behind the tool-search index); Crestodian channel listing was empty in packaged installs; setup approval now seeds the crestodian-scoped exec approval that local model harnesses require.

## User Impact

Fresh install → talk to a custodian with personality that already found your AI access; say yes; connect channels by chatting; meet your agent. Existing installs are untouched (config-authored setups keep opening the TUI/app; old app versions still get the classic wizard RPC; no config shape changes, no doctor migration needed).

## Evidence

- Unit/typecheck: `pnpm tsgo`, `pnpm check:test-types`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions` green; 165+ tests across `src/crestodian`, `src/agents/tools/crestodian-tool.test.ts`, `src/wizard`, `src/commands/onboard*`, `src/gateway/server-methods/crestodian.test.ts`, `src/cli/run-main.test.ts`; 18/18 Swift onboarding tests (incl. new permission-order regression) + `swift build`.
- Fresh-machine e2e (Parallels "macOS Tahoe", real `npm pack` tarball, isolated state): `openclaw onboard` → conversation with detection → **yes** wrote `openclaw.json` (model, gateway token) + workspace bootstrap files; `channels` lists 28 channels; `connect telegram` hosts the wizard in-chat.
- Live agent loop (host, Codex login, isolated state): custodian ran on the embedded loop via the Codex app-server harness, made 10 audited `crestodian` tool calls, reported real machine state, and proposed the next mutation behind approval.
- Verification loop live: `gateway.port = "banana"` → exact zod error into the chat; unknown key rejected; `config get gateway.auth` redacts the token; invalid-after-write drives an approval-gated fix proposal (unit-tested).
- Remote broad gate (`pnpm check:changed` via Testbox-through-Crabbox) started; Docker lanes `test:docker:crestodian-{first-run,planner,rescue}` should run in CI before merge. Known gap: claude-cli harness sessions use the planner fallback until the MCP tool bridge lands (follow-up filed).

target.title: refactor: extract reusable AI runtime package
target.body:
Closes #99040

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's model protocol adapters and streaming registry were embedded in the main application, so other packages could not reuse the proven Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Google, Vertex, Mistral, and ChatGPT/Codex transports without taking on OpenClaw's application runtime.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extracts one public package: `@openclaw/ai`. It contains the provider-neutral model/message/tool contracts, validation, diagnostics, event streams, isolated runtime registry, and lazy provider adapters. `packages/llm-core` remains a private implementation package and is bundled into `@openclaw/ai`; consumers never install or publish a second OpenClaw AI package.

The package is genuinely self-contained. Pure transport helpers that previously lived in application code (tool projections and strict-schema normalization, system-prompt cache boundary, stream first-event timeout, streaming byte guard, deferred event buffer, Anthropic model contract/refusal/auth-header helpers, OpenAI reasoning-effort and responses-stream compat, reasoning-tag text partitioner, LLM request activity) moved into `packages/ai`; `utf16-slice` moved into `@openclaw/normalization-core`. Host policy stays in OpenClaw and is injected through a narrow `AiTransportHost` port (`configureAiTransportHost`): guarded model fetch (SSRF policy), secret redaction for tool-result replay, OpenAI strict-tool defaults, and diagnostics logging. Library defaults are inert; `src/llm/stream.ts` installs OpenClaw's implementations. There are no relative imports from the package back into `src/`.

The public barrel is instance-first: `createApiRegistry()` / `createLlmRuntime()` plus contracts and the host port. The process-default registry/runtime and their bound helpers moved behind `@openclaw/ai/internal/*`, which exists for OpenClaw itself and carries no semver guarantee (documented in the README). `registerBuiltInApiProviders(registry)` takes an explicit registry. Built-in provider registration is table-driven, replacing ~420 lines of per-provider boilerplate.

OpenClaw consumes `@openclaw/ai` as a normal workspace dependency, which `pnpm pack` converts to the exact release version. Runtime stream construction resolves through `@openclaw/ai/event-stream`, preserving one `EventStream` constructor identity across OpenClaw, agent-core, and external consumers. The release workflow packs, verifies, and publishes `@openclaw/ai` before the root package, and `packages/ai` now ships its own `npm-shrinkwrap.json` so its transitive dependency tree stays pinned at user install time even though workspace deps are omitted from the root shrinkwrap.

## User Impact

Existing OpenClaw users should see no configuration, model selection, authentication, or streaming behavior change. Installing `openclaw` installs the exact `@openclaw/ai` release automatically, with the AI package's dependency tree pinned by its own shrinkwrap. Library consumers can depend on the one package, create isolated runtimes, and opt into the eight built-in API adapters without inheriting a mutable process-global registry.

## Evidence

- `pnpm build` passed end to end: package declarations, root bundle, CLI/bootstrap guards, runtime postbuild, plugin SDK export check, and Control UI build.
- `pnpm tsgo` and `pnpm check:test-types` pass; the `tsdown.config.ts` `dts.neverBundle` option was moved to its correct `deps.dts` home (the previous placement was a type error that broke `check-test-types` on CI).
- The `checks-node-compact-*` CI failures (`Cannot find module @openclaw/ai/dist/providers.mjs`) were root-caused to three Node-side alias tables that only knew `@openclaw/llm-core`: `src/plugin-sdk/root-alias.cjs`, `src/plugins/plugin-sdk-native-resolver.ts`, and `src/plugins/sdk-alias.ts`. All now cover the `@openclaw/ai` export map (and the new `normalization-core/utf16-slice` subpath); the previously failing tests (`models-config.applies-config-env-vars`, `model-selection`) pass locally.
- `check-dependencies` (knip) is clean: `packages/ai` declares only its six real runtime deps (Anthropic/OpenAI/Google/Mistral SDKs, partial-json, typebox); orphaned root deps (`@mistralai/mistralai`, `partial-json`) removed; knip config knows the new package's entry points.
- Focused suites pass locally via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`: all of `packages/ai`, `src/llm`, `packages/agent-core`, `packages/normalization-core`, transport streams, model selection/config, custom API registry, and the host-port integration proofs (SSRF fetch-proof, redaction contract, OpenAI-compatible auth) — 869 tests, 0 failures.
- `pnpm check:changed` run over the full branch diff.
- Fresh Codex autoreview completed clean with no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: Fix Android realtime tool completion synchronization
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android Talk Mode realtime tool calls tracked `realtimeToolRuns`, `pendingRealtimeToolCalls`, and `pendingRealtimeToolCompletions` in unsynchronized `LinkedHashMap`/`LinkedHashSet` state. Gateway chat events and `talk.client.toolCall` responses both run on `Dispatchers.IO`, so a terminal chat event could race run registration and leave an `openclaw_agent_consult` result stranded instead of submitting `talk.session.submitToolResult`.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change puts the realtime tool state transitions behind a dedicated `realtimeToolLock`. Run registration, pending terminal completion caching, cached completion consumption, stale-session checks, and run removal are now decided under the same lock. The actual gateway result/error submission still happens after releasing the lock, so the lock does not cover network I/O.

The patch also bounds cached realtime completions with the same cache cap used elsewhere in Talk Mode and adds a regression test for a final chat event arriving before run metadata exists.

## User Impact

Realtime Talk Mode should no longer hang on `openclaw_agent_consult` when the agent answer and tool-call RPC response arrive concurrently. Users should get the voice reply instead of staying stuck in `Thinking...` until the provider times out.

## Evidence

target.title: feat(release): add monthly npm extended-stable publication
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw cannot currently publish a trailing-month core package to the npm
`extended-stable` dist-tag without treating it like the existing promoted
`latest` channel or adopting the much larger superseded release-policy
framework. The existing Full Release Validation graph also rejects the required
`extended-stable/YYYY.M.33` workflow ref, making a guarded monthly run
unreachable.

The user-facing `stable` update channel already resolves through npm `latest`.
This PR intentionally uses the separate `extended-stable` name so the new
trailing-month contract does not redefine that existing channel.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one npm-only `extended-stable` mode to the existing release workflow.
Final `YYYY.M.PATCH` versions at patch `33` or later must publish from the exact
`extended-stable/YYYY.M.33` branch, with the release tag, checkout, branch tip,
package version, preflight run, Full Release Validation run, manifest, and
promoted tarball all bound to the same commit.

The implementation reuses the existing preflight manifest v1 and tested
tarball, captures the prior npm selector before mutation, performs bounded
exact-version and selector readback, and prints a forward repair command that
points `extended-stable` at the newly published version. Rollback to the prior
selector is a separate operator decision. Full Release Validation narrowly
trusts the canonical extended-stable branch shape and verifies every required
child run used the target SHA.

Plugin publication, native platforms, GitHub Releases, private dist-tags,
Docker, mobile, and website publication remain out of scope. Protected `main`
must be on any strictly later calendar month with a daily patch below `33`, so
supported maintenance patches remain publishable after development advances
more than one month.

Fork and non-production rehearsals can explicitly set
`bypass_extended_stable_guard=true` to relax the `.33` threshold and protected
`main` month policy. The bypass is extended-stable-only and default-off; it
still requires the canonical branch, branch-tip/tag/checkout SHA equality,
final tag/package identity, authenticated validation evidence, verified
tarball, environment approval, and registry proof.

## User Impact

Release operators can publish the completed month's core `openclaw` package to
npm `extended-stable`, beginning at `.33`, without moving `latest` or invoking
other publication surfaces. Maintainers can exercise the guarded path with a
historical test version by enabling the audited bypass. Existing user-facing
`stable | beta | dev` CLI channel behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Current head: `4c0a6e5fef`.

target.title: fix(gateway): defer hot-reload restart when dist/entry.js is missing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pushing commits into a live production git checkout triggers the gateway's hot-reload while `dist/` is mid-rebuild. The watcher (`requestRestart()` in `scripts/watch-node.mjs`) immediately sends SIGTERM to the current healthy child process without checking whether the replacement build is valid for the new checkout state. The new child cannot start → crash-loop until systemd's start-limit is exhausted (37-min outage, P1, issue #99603).

## Changes

Two guard points using `isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs, resolveHead)` in `scripts/watch-node.mjs`:

**Guard 1 — requestRestart()**: Before sending SIGTERM, verify `dist/entry.js` exists AND `dist/.buildstamp` git HEAD matches current checkout HEAD. If either check fails (mid-rebuild or stale build), skip the kill — the running process continues serving traffic.

**Guard 2 — Exit handler**: After SIGTERM/143 child exit, verify build readiness before restarting. Prevents self-reinforcing crash-loop.

**Scope**: Partial mitigation — prevents crash-loop but keeps stop-then-start ordering. Issue #99603 should remain open for transactional restart.

## Evidence

target.title: fix: reject unsupported custom tool_choice in OpenAI Responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When using the OpenAI provider with the Responses API, tool calls fail with error "Invalid value: 'custom'" because the `reconcileOpenAIResponsesToolChoice` function did not validate or reject `tool_choice` objects with `type: "custom"`.

The OpenAI Responses API does not support `{ type: "custom" }` tool choices. However, the OpenAI SDK types include this option, and without validation, such values were passed directly to the API, causing runtime errors.

**Issue**: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/99856

## Why This Change Was Made

The `reconcileOpenAICompletionsToolChoice` function already handled this case by throwing an error for `custom` types (lines 238-242). However, the corresponding `reconcileOpenAIResponsesToolChoice` function was missing this check, allowing invalid `{ type: "custom" }` values to reach the OpenAI Responses API.

This fix aligns the two functions and prevents invalid `tool_choice` values from causing API errors.

**Changes**:

1. **[src/agents/openai-tool-projection.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/agents/openai-tool-projection.ts)**
   - Created internal type `OpenAIResponsesSdkToolChoice` for the full SDK type (line 31)
   - Created exported type `OpenAIResponsesToolChoice` that excludes `{ type: "custom" }` (lines 36-39)
   - Changed `reconcileOpenAIResponsesToolChoice` parameter type to `OpenAIResponsesSdkToolChoice` (line 158)
   - Added runtime check in `reconcileOpenAIResponsesToolChoice` to throw error for `custom` types (lines 176-180)

2. **[src/agents/openai-transport-stream.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/agents/openai-transport-stream.ts)**
   - Imported new `OpenAIResponsesToolChoice` type (line 86)
   - Updated `OpenAIResponsesOptions.toolChoice` to use the narrower exported type (line 216)

3. **[src/agents/openai-tool-projection.test.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/agents/openai-tool-projection.test.ts)**
   - Added test case to verify `custom` type is correctly rejected by `reconcileOpenAIResponsesToolChoice` (lines 284-290)

## User Impact

- **Before**: Users passing `tool_choice: { type: "custom", name: "xxx" }` would receive cryptic "Invalid value: 'custom'" errors from OpenAI API
- **After**: Users receive a clear error message: "OpenAI Responses custom tool_choice is unsupported because this adapter emits function tools only"

Other valid `tool_choice` types (`"auto"`, `"required"`, `"none"`, `{ type: "function", name: "xxx" }`, `{ type: "allowed_tools", ... }`, and built-in tools like `web_search_preview`) continue to work as expected.

## Evidence

- ✅ `pnpm test src/agents/openai-tool-projection.test.ts` — 15 tests passed
- ✅ `pnpm test src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts` — 286 tests passed
- ✅ `pnpm test src/llm/providers/openai-completions.test.ts` — 37 tests passed
- ✅ `pnpm test src/llm/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts` — 34 tests passed
- ✅ `pnpm test src/gateway/openresponses-http.test.ts` — 93 tests passed

**Created from**: `openclaw/openclaw@bd2740fedc` (latest main)

target.title: fix(bedrock): bound Mantle model discovery fetches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users relying on Amazon Bedrock Mantle model discovery could have provider setup hang indefinitely when the `/v1/models` request stalls, or consume unbounded memory when the endpoint streams an oversized JSON body.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mantle model discovery now treats the provider catalog response as an untrusted network boundary: the fetch receives a 30 second abort signal, and successful JSON bodies are read through the existing bounded response reader with a 4 MiB cap. The 4 MiB cap matches OpenClaw's existing live model catalog body cap for provider-owned model catalogs; the larger 16 MiB setup-discovery cap is for self-hosted setup JSON, so this keeps the Mantle fix aligned with the live catalog path. The timeout/cap boundary preserves the existing failure behavior: discovery errors fall back to cached models or an empty result instead of hanging or reading an unbounded response.

No schema, config, migration, stored-state, or public provider contract is changed.

## User Impact

Mantle provider discovery is now bounded for normal, oversized, and stalled provider responses. Users should see provider resolution fail safely instead of hanging the process or reading an unbounded response body. If a Mantle catalog exceeds the bounded provider-catalog limit or does not produce a response within 30 seconds, discovery uses the same cache-or-empty fallback path it already used for provider failures.

## Evidence

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users routing OpenAI-compatible BYOK providers through the GitHub Copilot harness could hit upstream 401s when the Copilot SDK/runtime omitted the resolved bearer `Authorization` header before the loopback proxy forwarded the request.

This was reproduced with Tencent TokenPlan/TokenHub-shaped Chat Completions providers: direct OpenClaw provider calls succeeded, while the same provider/model through Copilot BYOK could fail at the upstream auth hop.

AI-assisted: yes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Copilot BYOK proxy now carries OpenClaw's resolved bearer auth intent to the final SSRF-guarded upstream hop, but only for nonce-protected proxy requests and only when the SDK did not already send `authorization`. Azure SDK nonce-less `/openai/...` proxy paths remain excluded so discovering the loopback port cannot turn the proxy into a bearer-token relay.

The package install proof also confirms the existing `@github/copilot-sdk` production dependency resolves the Copilot CLI package transitively, so this PR does not change the plugin dependency graph.

## User Impact

Users can run Tencent TokenPlan/TokenHub and Ollama Cloud OpenAI-compatible BYOK models through the Copilot harness without losing bearer auth at the proxy hop. The PR does not change the plugin dependency graph; the existing SDK dependency continues to resolve the Copilot CLI package in production installs.

target.title: fix: skip volatile backup cache paths
target.body:
Fixes #98865

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw backup create` could still traverse disposable agent runtime caches, browser cache/resource-cache trees, retired archive copies, and state-side transient sidecars. Those paths can bloat archives or race with tar even though they have no restoration value.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing backup archive path already centralizes volatile filtering through `isVolatileBackupPath`, so this extends that owner boundary instead of adding another archive-time special case. Browser filtering is intentionally scoped to cache-like directories under managed `user-data` paths so durable profile files such as `Preferences` and `Login Data` remain eligible for backup. `.lock` and `.partial` files are scoped to cache, queue, and tmp scratch roots so installed plugin source under `state/extensions` stays backed up; SQLite sidecars stay under the backup SQLite snapshot consistency guard instead of being treated as generic volatile files.

Issue #98865 was closed manually rather than by a merged runtime fix. I checked current `upstream/main`, the issue closure events, and related PR search; I found a docs-only open PR (#99007) but no equivalent runtime fix on main.

## User Impact

Backups now skip more disposable runtime/cache files and retired archive copies, reducing archive size and avoiding avoidable live-file races while preserving durable OpenClaw state, browser profile data, installed plugin source files, and SQLite consistency checks.

## Evidence

Current head: `80b7e213c41e7b2d2a24af70584489ef34c13bb8`.

Scope follow-up: this PR is now backup-only again. The unrelated QA-lab Crabline readiness timeout follow-up was removed from the branch so maintainers only need to review the backup archive payload boundary.

Claim proved: the backup path skips disposable cache/runtime/archive sidecars while preserving durable browser profile files, installed plugin files, and SQLite snapshot consistency behavior.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/backup-volatile-filter.test.ts`  
  Result: passed, 61 tests.

  Result: passed, 3 tests, 36 skipped. This covers the CI failure where `late.sqlite-wal` must still trigger the SQLite snapshot retry error instead of being swallowed by the volatile filter, plus the volatile skip-count summary.

target.title: fix(failover): provider refusals now trigger the model fallback chain
target.body:
Fixes #98976

## What Problem This Solves
Provider refusals (Anthropic `refusal`/`sensitive` stop reasons, OpenAI `content_filter` finish_reason) were never classified as a distinct FailoverReason. They fell through to the generic `LLM request failed` error path, bypassing the model fallback chain entirely — no retry on the next configured model, no auth-profile distinction, and confusing user-facing error text.

## Evidence
256 tests pass across all fix-relevant suites, including the new `anthropic-refusal.test.ts` and updated `openai-stop-reason.test.ts`, `result-fallback-classifier.test.ts`, `errors.test.ts`, `failover-matches.test.ts`, `run/failover-policy.test.ts`, `auth-profile-failure-policy.test.ts`, `failover-policy.test.ts`, `anthropic.test.ts`, `anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts`, and `packages/llm-core/types.test.ts`.

This fix has also been running in production on four independent gateway instances (Newhart, Victoria, Graybeard, NOVA) since 2026-07-03 with no regressions. All four instances are verified healthy on this change.

## Root cause
Provider refusals (Anthropic `refusal`/`sensitive` stop reasons, OpenAI `content_filter` finish_reason) were never classified as a distinct FailoverReason. They fell through to the generic `LLM request failed` error path, bypassing the model fallback chain entirely — no retry on the next configured model, no auth-profile distinction, and confusing user-facing error text.

## Fix summary

- **New `refusal` FailoverReason** added to the `AgentRuntimeFailoverReason` union. `errorCode: "provider_refusal"` is set at the Anthropic and OpenAI transport layers.
- **Transport normalization:** Anthropic `sensitive` stop reason is treated like `refusal`; OpenAI `content_filter` maps to `errorCode: "provider_refusal"`.
- **No auth-profile rotation.** Refusals are content-scoped, not credential-scoped — the policy layer never rotates auth profiles or puts them in cooldown for a refusal.
- **No same-model retry.** The fallback skips the current model and moves to the next candidate directly.
- **Preserved probe budget.** Refusals do not consume the transient cooldown probe slot.
- **Partial-output detection.** If the model produced visible output before refusing, the output is surfaced as an error instead of silently retrying on another model (avoiding duplicate/contradictory replies).
- **Stable user copy.** When a refusal is surfaced, the user sees: *"The model declined to generate this response. Try rephrasing your request, or switch to a different model."*
- **PR #94430 boundary.** `refusal` classification takes precedence over `rate_limit` in the shared error classifier. Overlap is minimal — #94430 targets different error text patterns. A boundary comment has been added in `errors.ts`.

## Test coverage
256 tests pass across all fix-relevant suites:
| Area | Tests | Status |
|------|-------|--------|
| `anthropic-refusal.test.ts` (new) | 5 | ✅ |
| `openai-stop-reason.test.ts` | 8 | ✅ |
| `result-fallback-classifier.test.ts` | 23 | ✅ |
| `errors.test.ts` | 13 | ✅ |
| `failover-matches.test.ts` | 36 | ✅ |
| `run/failover-policy.test.ts` | 39 | ✅ |
| `auth-profile-failure-policy.test.ts` | 8 | ✅ |
| `failover-policy.test.ts` | 1 | ✅ |
| `anthropic.test.ts` (incl. sensitive regression) | 39 | ✅ |
| `anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` (incl. sensitive regression) | 83 | ✅ |
| `packages/llm-core/types.test.ts` | 1 | ✅ |

## Production validation
This fix has been running in production on four independent gateway instances (Newhart, Victoria, Graybeard, NOVA) since 2026-07-03 with no regressions. All four instances are verified healthy on this change.

## Maintainer notes
This PR carries a `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr` label on the issue — the fix has been through staging testing (356 tests, green) and production validation across multiple gateways. We are filing this upstream as a fully tested, validated fix for the maintainer-review path (`needs-maintainer-review` / `needs-security-review`). All changes are scoped to failover policy, transport normalization, and user-facing copy — no architectural impact outside the fallback classifier and failover policy layers.

We defer entirely to maintainer judgment on whether the approach and implementation are appropriate for upstream. Happy to adjust scope, naming, or any other aspect per review feedback.

## Real behavior proof

### Expected behavior
When a provider returns a content-policy refusal (e.g. Anthropic `refusal`/`sensitive` stop reason, OpenAI `content_filter` finish reason), the runner should treat this as a non-auth, non-retryable failure that walks the model fallback chain. The refusal classification must preserve any partial assistant output already delivered to the user, must not retry the same model, and must not poison shared auth-profile health.

### Actual behavior (before fix)
Provider content-policy refusals were classified as generic `unclassified` errors. This caused:
- The fallback chain to stop instead of trying the next model.
- Partial outputs from a refused turn to be discarded.
- In some configurations, the refusal could be treated as an auth failure and cool down a healthy profile.

### Repro steps
1. Configure a model that uses Anthropic (`claude-sonnet-4-6`) or OpenAI (`gpt-4.1`) and trigger a content-policy refusal.
2. Ensure a fallback model is configured in the agent/model chain.
3. Observe that before the fix the run terminates with `unclassified`; after the fix the run advances to the next model with `reason: "refusal"` and `code: "provider_refusal"`.

### Test evidence
Local verification against upstream `main` after rebase:
- `pnpm tsgo:prod` — passed
- `pnpm tsgo:test` — passed
- `pnpm lint` — passed
- `vitest.agents-embedded-agent.config.ts` — 85 files, 1605 tests passed
- `vitest.cron.config.ts` — 117 files, 1232 tests passed
- `vitest.shared-core.config.ts` — 10 files, 73 tests passed

Note: `agents-core` and `agents-support` configs show unrelated pre-existing failures in `anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts`, `cli-runner.reliability.test.ts`, `code-mode.test.ts`, `compaction-planning-worker.test.ts`, `minimax-docs.test.ts`, `model-catalog.test.ts`, `openai-transport-stream.test.ts`, `transport-params-runtime-contract.test.ts`, `auth-profiles/oauth.openai-codex-refresh-fallback.test.ts`, and `harness/runtime-plugin.test.ts`. The touched files all pass.

target.title: docs: clarify plugin package live proof
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a documentation gap where plugin authors and maintainers could conflate source/archive installs, `npm-pack:` package proof, and trusted official plugin proof when validating plugin packages. That made it easy to miss runtime dependency mistakes or to overstate what a local tarball install proves for privileged plugin behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds package/live-proof guidance in the OpenClaw testing skill and clarifies the plugin docs. The docs now separate managed package dependency proof via `npm-pack:` from catalog-linked official trust proof, and the plugin quickstart now calls out runtime dependency ownership plus the need for built JavaScript entries before package-install validation.

## User Impact

Plugin authors and reviewers get a clearer path for validating release-candidate plugin packages. They can catch dependencies left in `devDependencies`, avoid manual repairs inside managed npm projects as final proof, and know when privileged official plugin behavior needs a second trusted install proof.

## Evidence

- `pnpm docs:check-links`

- `git diff --check`

target.title: fix(codex): warn when routes use stale embedded binaries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can look current while `/codex` routes still spawn the stale `@openai/codex` bundled inside the active `@openclaw/codex` plugin. Fleet evidence in #99951 shows one customer VM and one reference VM running `@openclaw/codex@2026.6.11` with nested `@openai/codex@0.139.0`, even though the host/global `codex` CLI is newer and `openclaw plugins update codex --dry-run` reports the plugin current.

This is a stable-channel false green, not a beta-only problem. Read-only npm checks on 2026-07-04 showed:

```text
@openclaw/codex@2026.6.5          -> @openai/codex 0.135.0
@openclaw/codex@2026.6.6          -> @openai/codex 0.139.0
@openclaw/codex@2026.6.8          -> @openai/codex 0.139.0
@openclaw/codex@2026.6.9          -> @openai/codex 0.139.0
@openclaw/codex@2026.6.10         -> @openai/codex 0.139.0
@openclaw/codex@2026.6.11-beta.2  -> @openai/codex 0.139.0
@openclaw/codex@2026.6.11         -> @openai/codex 0.139.0
@openclaw/codex@2026.7.1-beta.1   -> @openai/codex 0.142.4
@openai/codex@latest              -> 0.142.5
```

So normal stable/customer updates can keep the primary Codex provider route on the old app-server runtime even while beta has moved forward.

## Why This Change Was Made

`codex --version` on the host is not route health proof. Upstream Codex launches its platform binary from the installed `@openai/codex` package tree, so OpenClaw’s `/codex` route truth must come from the active plugin package root and its vendored runtime dependency.

The missed Codex release surface between `0.139.0` and `0.142.5` includes changes that overlap with OpenClaw's embedded app-server route path:

- `0.142.5`: trace/logging safety fix preventing full Responses WebSocket request payloads from being written to trace logs.
- `0.142.2`: MCP tool-search behavior, remote plugin catalog fixes, remote stdio cwd handling, remote image validation, PowerShell safety approval handling, and patched bundled dependencies.
- `0.141.x` / `0.140.x`: app-server/session/state/auth/reliability changes, exec-server and shell behavior fixes, plugin/MCP reliability improvements, and thread/session durability fixes.

This PR does not claim every Codex route symptom is caused by the stale binary. It closes the release-gate gap that allowed OpenClaw to report current while running a stale primary-provider route runtime.

This PR:

- bumps the Codex provider runtime dependency to `@openai/codex@0.142.5`;
- reports plugin version, declared runtime dependency, installed runtime dependency, and plugin root in status/doctor drift surfaces;
- warns/fails when active `@openclaw/codex` embeds a stale or missing `@openai/codex` route runtime;
- makes exact-pinned stale route-runtime remediation suggest `openclaw plugins update @openclaw/codex` instead of an id-only update that can preserve the stale pin;
- adds plugin publish/pretag guards so packed `@openclaw/codex` shrinkwrap/platform aliases must match the approved route runtime dependency.

## User Impact

Operators get a visible release-blocking warning when OpenClaw’s Codex provider route would run an older embedded Codex binary than the approved release expects. This does not claim customer fleets are remediated; it proves detection/blocking and requires a later approved rollout to fix customer VMs.

## Evidence

Issue/evidence:

- Release blocker issue: #99951
- OpenAI Codex changelog: https://developers.openai.com/codex/changelog
- `@openai/codex` npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/%40openai/codex
- `@openclaw/codex` npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/%40openclaw/codex
- Evidence packet: `internal redacted evidence packet (private; available to maintainers on request)`
- Dependency report: `/Volumes/LEXAR/Codex/codex-openclaw-route-version-checks/pr-99956/dependency-changes.md`
- Redacted stale-route status proof: `/Volumes/LEXAR/Codex/codex-openclaw-route-version-checks/pr-99956/status-deep-stale-route-runtime-proof.txt`

Real npm-installed stale route package proof (registry install, lifecycle scripts disabled):

```json
{
  "source": "npm install --ignore-scripts --omit=dev @openclaw/codex@2026.6.11",
  "plugin": {
    "name": "@openclaw/codex",
    "version": "2026.6.11",
    "declaredOpenAiCodex": "0.139.0"
  },
  "nestedRuntime": {
    "name": "@openai/codex",
    "version": "0.139.0",
    "bin": {
      "codex": "bin/codex.js"
    }
  }
}
```

Redacted `openclaw status --deep` renderer proof against that npm-installed `@openclaw/codex@2026.6.11` package root:

```text
Service: openclaw-gateway (loaded)

Gateway version: 2026.6.11

Connectivity probe: ok

Plugin version drift: 1 route runtime dependency not on the approved release version
- codex in 2026.6.11: @openai/codex 0.139.0 (npm) → expected 0.142.5
  Plugin root: <lexar-evidence-root>/real-npm-stale-install/node_modules/@openclaw/codex
  Runtime package: <lexar-evidence-root>/real-npm-stale-install/node_modules/@openclaw/codex/node_modules/@openai/codex/package.json
Fix: openclaw plugins update @openclaw/codex && openclaw gateway restart.

Troubles: run openclaw status
Troubleshooting: https://docs.openclaw.ai/troubleshooting
```

Focused local validation:

- `pnpm install --lockfile-only --ignore-scripts`
- `pnpm exec node scripts/generate-npm-shrinkwrap.mjs --package-dir extensions/codex`
- `node scripts/generate-npm-shrinkwrap.mjs --package-dir extensions/codex --check`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 ...`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.scripts.json scripts/lib/plugin-npm-release.ts`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/plugins/plugin-version-drift.ts src/plugins/plugin-version-drift.test.ts src/cli/daemon-cli/status.print.ts src/commands/doctor-workspace-status.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/plugin-version-drift.test.ts src/cli/daemon-cli/status.print.test.ts src/commands/doctor-workspace-status.test.ts extensions/codex/src/manifest.test.ts test/plugin-npm-release.test.ts`
- `pnpm tsgo:test:src`

Dependency-guard boundary:

- This PR intentionally changes `extensions/codex/package.json`, `extensions/codex/npm-shrinkwrap.json`, and `pnpm-lock.yaml` for the `@openai/codex` family from `0.142.4` to `0.142.5`.
